topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This topic frames the final lecture by outlining the learning objectives regarding cancer therapy approaches and mechanisms.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and resistance mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss standard treatment modalities including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy, alongside the problem of systemic toxicity and drug efflux pumps.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic cancer cell vulnerabilities and defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover strategies that selectively target cancer cell weaknesses, including hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint deficiencies, and DNA repair defects.

topics.label: Targeted kinase inhibitors and acquired resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine small molecule inhibitors directed against driver oncogenes and kinases, as well as the molecular pathways causing drug resistance and addiction.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibody and antibody-drug conjugate therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the design and application of therapeutic monoclonal antibodies that block receptors, mediate immune cytotoxicity, or deliver targeted toxins.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and T-cell-directed strategies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore approaches for harnessing the patient's immune system against tumors, ranging from immune surveillance and checkpoint inhibitors to bispecific antibodies and CAR T cells.

topics.label: Therapeutic challenges, historical progress, and future directions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the broader landscape of cancer treatment by reviewing therapy limitations, historical survival trends, emerging approaches, and clinical decision-making.
